directive: **Configure** — right after Discovery, decide which OPTIONAL capabilities this project needs and record them with `bsc plan classify set` (a JSON object on stdin). From the discovery findings + the pitch, determine: (1) `uiMode` — `custom` if the UI is generated IN-APP (the designer builds a live, navigable shell you preview as you plan — the default for most apps) or `external` if the user brings their own design files to drop in; (2) which of the OFF-by-default optional stages the project genuinely needs — `needsSource` (migrating data FROM a legacy system: a CRM/ERP/SaaS/database), `needsMcp` (the fleet's agents need external tools or data via MCP servers), `needsSkills` (a reusable skill library is worth authoring for this project), `needsAutomations` (scheduled / cron jobs). MOST projects need NONE of the optional stages — turn one on ONLY if the project truly requires it, and ASK the user to confirm before enabling. Examples: `{"uiMode":"custom"}` for a simple app; `{"uiMode":"custom","needsSource":true}` for a data migration. Enabling a stage makes it appear in the plan for you to complete. Then, having settled the app-type + optional stages, DECLARE this app's key CONTRACTS — the OTHER apps, external services, or MCP servers it depends on / talks to — with `bsc project link add <this-project-key> <endpoint> <api|data|events> --target-type project|service|mcp` (add `--app-type <type>` for a service/mcp endpoint, e.g. `api` or `serverless`), so the relationship shows in Glance and downstream agents know the contract. Record ONLY real dependencies. Example: `bsc project link add my-app stripe api --target-type service --url https://api.stripe.com --app-type api`. Gate: the classification is recorded.

blurb: Decide which optional capabilities the project needs — integrations, MCP servers, skills, automations — plus the UI mode.
prompt:
Right after Discovery, decide which OPTIONAL capabilities this project needs and record them with
`bsc plan classify set` (a JSON object on stdin). Set `uiMode` (`custom` = an in-app generated UI, the
default; `external` = the user brings their own design files). Then enable ONLY the optional stages the
project genuinely needs: `needsSource` (migrating from a legacy system), `needsMcp` (agents need external
tools via MCP servers), `needsSkills` (a reusable skill library), `needsAutomations` (scheduled jobs).
Most projects need none of these — ASK the user to confirm before turning one on. Enabling a stage makes
it appear in the plan.

Then, with the app-type + optional stages settled, DECLARE this app's key CONTRACTS — the OTHER apps,
external services, or MCP servers it depends on / talks to — so the relationship shows in Glance and the
fleet knows the contract:

  bsc project link add <this-project-key> <endpoint> <api|data|events> --target-type project|service|mcp

For a service or MCP endpoint add `--app-type <type>` (e.g. `api`, `serverless`) and, when known, `--url`.
Record ONLY real dependencies. Example:

  bsc project link add my-app stripe api --target-type service --url https://api.stripe.com --app-type api

Gate: the classification is recorded.
